hook.en: Rice is harvested in a few weeks but eaten every day of the year. Somewhere in between, it waits in a warehouse.

say.en: Rice is harvested in a few weeks but eaten every day of the year. Somewhere in between, it waits in a warehouse. In this lesson: Classify warehouses.
Explain the functions of warehousing.

body.en: Private *warehouses* are owned by manufacturers or traders for their own goods. Public warehouses are licensed by the government and rent space to anyone. Bonded warehouses store imported goods until customs duty is paid. Government warehouses are run by bodies such as the Central Warehousing Corporation, and cooperative warehouses are owned by cooperative societies.

say.en: Warehouses are classified by who owns them and who uses them.
A bonded warehouse holds imported goods until customs duty is paid. Government and cooperative warehouses complete the list.
Consolidation: goods from several plants are collected in one warehouse. Break bulk: big lots are split for many shops.
It also stockpiles seasonal goods, adds value by packing and grading, stabilises prices, and its receipt can be pledged for a loan.
Above all, warehousing removes the hindrance of time.

narration.en: Rice is harvested in three months but eaten all year. With a warehouse the surplus is stored and released month by month; without one, the market runs dry after the harvest.

problem.en: A trader stores 500 quintals of tur dal in a public warehouse at ₹4 per quintal per month for 6 months. He pledges the warehouse receipt for a bank loan. (a) Find the storage charge. (b) Name the two functions of warehousing used.

steps.en: Holding the dal for six months and releasing it later: stock piling (removes the hindrance of time).
Pledging the warehouse receipt for a loan: financing.

narration.en: Let us work through this case together. A trader stores 500 quintals of tur dal in a public warehouse at ₹4 per quintal per month for 6 months. He pledges the warehouse receipt for a bank loan. (a) Find the storage charge. (b) Name the two functions of warehousing used.

say.en: Let us work through this case together. A trader stores 500 quintals of tur dal in a public warehouse at 4 rupees per quintal per month for 6 months. He pledges the warehouse receipt for a bank loan. a Find the storage charge. b Name the two functions of warehousing used.
Storage charge equals 500 times 4 rupees times 6 equals 12,000 rupees.
Holding the dal for six months and releasing it later: stock piling (removes the hindrance of time).
Pledging the warehouse receipt for a loan: financing.
So the answer is 12,000 rupees; stock piling and financing.
